style: drawing-first graphite and selective ink with loose restrained watercolor and colored-pencil pigment; visible sketch construction; natural adult anatomy; no glossy, faceted, mosaic, or low-poly rendering
continuity_floor: Greg is nineteen, has a permanent left below-knee amputation with knee preserved and right leg intact, and uses two crutches; Lyssa is a tall, thin Black woman with natural Afro-textured hair
contact_sheet_scope: first 25 items; remaining 5 retained in manifest and reader

items.anchor: The first thing backstage did was try to kill me with a painted tree.
items.alt: Greg braces on two crutches as a painted stage tree tips through the busy backstage space.

items.anchor: rehearsal could not continue until I got there
items.alt: Greg joins a crowded rehearsal as a stand-in while actors and crew wait around the stage.

items.anchor: predictable enough to affect sightlines
items.alt: Greg sits with his crutches beside him while theatre workers adjust a rehearsal around his sightline.

items.anchor: under the lodging awning and built the route
items.alt: Greg studies a rain-soaked Carrow street from beneath an awning before setting out on two crutches.

items.anchor: through a wide door
items.alt: Greg climbs a broad theatre loading ramp on two crutches while scenery moves around him.

items.anchor: Pessa stepped into the open left side.
items.alt: Greg redirects between training stakes as Pessa blocks the open side of his route.

items.anchor: sat in the dragged chair holding a page
items.alt: Greg reads from a dragged chair while backstage fabric and workers stream past a nearby effect fire.

items.anchor: chair off to the side of the stage
items.alt: Greg sits at the side of the stage with pages in hand, ready to prompt the rehearsal.

items.anchor: rough circle in the dirt
items.alt: Pessa marks a dirt circle while Greg prepares to move through it on his crutches.

items.anchor: caught more weight through the other crutch and right leg
items.alt: Greg catches a slipping crutch by driving his weight through the other crutch and intact right leg.

items.anchor: Jorren put his forehead on the table.
items.alt: Jorren folds over the four-door game table after losing while Greg watches.

items.anchor: The seam rubbed exactly where the crutch
items.alt: A theatre dresser checks Greg's green shirt where its seam rubs against his crutch.

items.anchor: Cutting an onion with one hand
items.alt: Greg works out how to cut an onion while keeping stable support in a cramped kitchen.

items.anchor: I am not coming up there
items.alt: Greg reads from the front row with pages in hand while the rehearsal continues onstage.

items.anchor: My dearest Alina
items.alt: A rehearsal stops over two nearly identical red-sealed prop letters as Greg follows the page.

items.anchor: The repaired doorway shifted during the next run.
items.alt: A repaired stage doorway shifts during rehearsal as Greg and the company react.

items.anchor: The dot sat on the back of my right hand
items.alt: A small charcoal target sits below Greg's right little-finger knuckle during Hessa's assessment.

items.anchor: Hessa said, “Stop.”
items.alt: Hessa calls a stop as Greg holds still during the controlled forearm test.

items.anchor: Then your wrist moved.
items.alt: Hessa watches Greg's wrist closely after a small involuntary movement changes the test.

items.anchor: The patch sharpened at the upper edge.
items.alt: Greg and Hessa watch the wrong edge of a small shaped patch sharpen during the repeat test.

items.anchor: Deliberately reduce a small shaped alteration
items.alt: Greg repeats a careful shaping test at Hessa's table while maintaining an underlying draw.

items.anchor: Jorren tested the balance.
items.alt: Jorren tests a knife's balance at a crowded shop counter while Greg observes.

items.anchor: She set it on the opposite side of the room.
items.alt: Hessa carries one of Greg's crutches to the opposite side of the assessment room.

items.anchor: kissed my cheek, and left again
items.alt: Lyssa turns back through the theatre bustle to kiss Greg's cheek before leaving.

items.anchor: Hessa was eating bread.
items.alt: Hessa eats bread at her worktable while Greg waits with his crutches.

items.anchor: Hessa had two copper strips.
items.alt: Two narrow copper strips lie ready on Hessa's assessment table in front of Greg.

items.anchor: Right hand left the towel and took the right crutch grip.
items.alt: Greg transfers his right hand from the test towel to the right crutch grip under Hessa's observation.

items.anchor: somewhere to be only after I finished lunch
items.alt: Greg pauses over fish and flatbread before beginning his courier route through Carrow.

items.anchor: It hit the floor, bounced once, and rolled under the table.
items.alt: A dropped rehearsal cup bounces and rolls under a table as Greg and the actors react.

items.anchor: She took my arm for exactly two steps
items.alt: Lyssa releases Greg's arm after realizing the gesture interferes with his crutch movement.
